messages:
maya: @jonah heads-up — customer Acme reports a 502 from /v1/chat. They captured an `x-request-id` in the response: `req-20260314-9f3b`. Happened 2026-03-14T10:03:12Z in eu-west-1. Asking if we can pull server logs for that req id and confirm root cause. Curl they sent below.

jonah: thanks — can you paste the exact header and body they sent? also, which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)? retention differs by type.

maya: they included curl and short response. copying:

```bash
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req-20260314-9f3b" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}'
```

response snippet: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: req-20260314-9f3b
Content-Type: application/json` — no body, just timeout. Customer says this is intermittent (3/3 calls failed). They are hosted (self-serve).

jonah: ok. First pass query to run in Kibana / internal log UI: search across runtime + edge indices. Example query: 

```
index: redwood-runtime-*,redwood-edge-*
message: "req-20260314-9f3b" OR request_id: "req-20260314-9f3b" OR trace_id: "req-20260314-9f3b"
| sort @timestamp desc
```

For hosted customers retention is 30d; this is within retention. If you don't find it in runtime, check the edge index (edge logs show upstream timeout) and also filter by region: `region:eu-west-1`.

ingrid: note — logs for the API gateway (frontend) and the runtime (model host) live in different clusters. If Kibana returns nothing, provide me the exact request_id and I can run a deeper cross-cluster search (`project:hosted AND request_id:req-20260314-9f3b`). Also double-check whether the customer used proxy or CDN that might rewrite headers.

alex: can we ask the customer for a debug bundle and a repro curl that includes a timing header? e.g. ask them to run: 

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req-20260314-9f3b" \
  -H "X-Debug: 1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' 
```

Tell them to attach the full verbose output and set `include_debug_bundle=true` in the support form so we can correlate local timing with server traces.

maya: pinged customer for debug bundle and verbose curl. They also provided their tenant id: `acct-acme-42`. I told them to include the three failing req ids (they have 3) and the timestamps.

support-bot: FYI: log-retention policy — hosted: 30 days, dedicated: 45 days, private/on-prem: customer-controlled. Use `#logs-retention` for more info.

jonah: if you get the debug bundle and we still don't see entries, run internal `logsearch` helper (internal-only):

```
logsearch --projects redwood-runtime,redwood-edge --q "request_id:req-20260314-9f3b OR trace_id:req-20260314-9f3b" --from 2026-03-14T09:50:00Z --to 2026-03-14T10:10:00Z
```

That includes time window and both clusters. If that returns only gateway logs with a 502 upstream timeout, forward them to SRE & runtime oncall for model host investigation.

alex: ok — I'll keep this thread updated once customer uploads bundle. tagging @ingrid for cross-cluster run when we have ids. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — collecting bundle now, will upload here when complete.
